newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran attacks Bonn "interference" over journalist.
newsitem.headline: Iran attacks Bonn "interference" over journalist.

text.p: Iran criticised what it called German interference over the fate of an Iranian journalist arrested while trying to leave Iran this month, state Tehran Radio reported on Thursday.
It quoted foreign ministry spokesman Mahmoud Mohammadi as saying the arrest and trial of Faraj Sarkuhi was an internal affair and any foreign interference was "unacceptable."
"The arrest and trials of criminals including Sarkuhi is a common matter related to the internal affairs of Iran and any foreign interference in this matter is unacceptable," he said.
"We cannot be pressured by foreign political propaganda to disregard our principles and laws in the case of a person who has commited serious offences," Mohammadi added.
The radio said Sarkuhi's brother was arrested with him.
Bonn said on Tuesday its ambassador in Tehran was told Sarkuhi was arrested in southwest Iran on February 2 while trying to leave the country illegally.
A German foreign ministry spokesman said documents provided by Iran to prove Sarkuhi visited Germany last year -- when he says he was being tortured in detention -- were probably false.

Sarkuhi, the editor of the monthly Adineh (Friday) magazine, was one of six Iranian writers held briefly after security agents burst into a dinner function at the Tehran home of the German cultural attache Jens Gust in July. Iran expressed regret over the incident after Bonn protested the action.

Germany asked Iran for details of Sarkuhi's whereabouts following reports last week that he had not only been detained and tortured for 47 days last year when he was supposedly in Germany, but had now been arrested again.
The German spokesman said Bonn still wanted Iran to comment on these allegations, made in a letter from Sarkuhi which was published in several German newspapers.
Sarkuhi said in the letter, which Bonn believes is genuine, he had been held by the Iranian secret service and tortured into confessing in a taped interview that he had spied for Germany.

He said he believed Iran intends to use the confession in a row with Germany over an accusation by German prosecutors that Iranian leaders ordered the killing of three Kurdish dissidents and their translator in Berlin in 1992. An Iranian and four Lebanese are being tried for the killings. Iran denies any involvement.
